attributes.residual: fuzzy 85.5461% -> 95.6052%; real 871 -> 869; instruction count 576/575 -> 576/575; opcode multiset 9t -> 5t; frame 344 -> 592 = EXACTLY the target's 592. The pipelining residual named by the prior pass is CLOSED: every one of the ~40 SWAP expansions now emits the target's strict single-register r0 lbz/stb alternation, instruction for instruction. ONE mechanism remains and it accounts for essentially all of real 869. Per-callee-saved-register use counts are IDENTICAL to the target but rotated one register lower: ours r23=7 r24=42 r25=3 r26=4 r27=2 r28=4, target r23=0 r24=7 r25=42 r26=3 r27=3 r28=4. The rotation is caused by ONE extra live web we carry and the target does not: at 0x3a4 MWCC hoists `addi r27,r24,54` (blob + offsetof(AtreeDefinition,objectIndex)) to the top of the per-match-entry loop body and keeps that address live in a callee-saved register across the entire ~1200-byte loop body, including several calls, purely to serve the loop-tail store; the target forms no such address and stores with the fused displacement `sth r24,54(r25)`. Because stmw/lmw save a CONTIGUOUS range, that one extra web makes our save area start at r23/556 instead of the target's r24/560, which shifts all 239 stack slots down by exactly 4 bytes - so every stack access in the function reads as a diff line even though its opcode and register are correct. Kill the extra web and the frame base, all 239 displacements, and the register numbering all align at once. THREE distinct source forms were tried against it and all three produced byte-identical output (`addi r27,r24,54` unmoved, stmw r23 unmoved): (1) typed member write `((AtreeDefinition*)blob)->objectIndex = (s16)model` alone; (2) that plus the SWAP16 site as `*(u16*)&((AtreeDefinition*)blob)->objectIndex`; (3) that plus the SWAP16 site with the address-of removed entirely, `SWAP16(((AtreeDefinition*)blob)->objectIndex)`. Per-axis cap reached - DO NOT RETRY these three forms. Genuinely new ideas only: splitting the loop so the objectIndex store is not live across the calls, sinking the SWAP16 of objectIndex to sit adjacent to the store, or a WebFrank renaming-bisimulation rule (note that such a rule must also rewrite the stmw/lmw base and every r1 displacement, so it is NOT a pure register renaming and needs its own guard audit). Two smaller vetoed clusters also remain: the +2 li / -2 mr live-zero remat at the match-list preheader (law-vetoed, untouched) and a 1-instruction `mr r3,r30` vs `addi r3,r30,0` return-copy form at the epilogue.
